subject: Capacity contingency & burst entitlements — SynergyAI Dedicated deal
messages:
From: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@synergyai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T14:32:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated sizing question — burst SLAs and entitlements

Hi Neha / Ben,

Quick context: we're finalizing the internal approval packet for the Dedicated commit and the procurement team asked for a clear statement about what "burst entitlements" look like during quarterly peaks. Specifically they want:

- Maximum sustained burst (GPUs) we can request for a 4-hour window
- How burst interacts with our reserved slab (eviction vs. overtime lanes)
- Any guaranteed failover to other regions or model variants if Dedicated pool is saturated

Can you share the typical guardrails and any precedent you have for credits if burst is constrained? Attaching our usage profile and expected seasonal peaks.

Thanks,
Carlos
VP Product, SynergyAI

Attachment: synergy-expected-peaks.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@synergyai.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-20T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question — burst SLAs and entitlements

Hi Carlos — thanks for the details and the usage file. High-level answers below; Ben and Aditya are looping in for the engineering and commercial specifics.

Short answers (TL;DR):
- Max sustained burst: we typically allow a negotiated burst pool up to 2.0–3.5x of the committed slab for short windows (1–6 hours), depending on GPU type and account priority.
- Behavior: burst consumes ephemeral pool capacity; eviction only occurs if higher-priority reserved workloads need resources. We provide automatic fallback to a compatible quantized model variant and can route to a different region if configured in the contract.
- Credits: when we cannot meet burst due to fleet-wide constraints, we offer pro-rated burst credits for the impacted period as part of the SLA amendment.

Action items:
1) Ben: can you open a quick capacity model with the Synergy CSV and propose a 4-hour and 24-hour burst profile?
2) Aditya: commercial — recommend a burst entitlement band and credit schedule to include in the draft SLA.

I'll start a short draft SLA clause and share a version for review.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Sr. Director, Sales — Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@synergyai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-21T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question — burst SLAs and entitlements

On Mon, Sep 20, 2026 at 5:05 PM Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Carlos — thanks for the details and the usage file. High-level answers below; Ben and Aditya are looping in for the engineering and commercial specifics.

Thanks — dug into the CSV and ran a quick capacity model. Key engineering notes:

- Baseline: your committed slab (as listed) corresponds to 24 A100-equivalent GPUs sustained.
- Recommended burst profile:
  * Short burst (up to 4 hours): +2.5x (i.e., up to 60 GPUs) — viable if we reserve ~10% of regional ephemeral pool for Synergy during business-critical windows.
  * Medium burst (4–24 hours): +1.5x with a runway policy (soft-eviction after 8 hours).
  * Long surge (24+ hours): treat as a temporary commit increase — requires pre-approval and capacity procurement.
- Fallback behavior: route to quantized variant (8-bit) with minor expected latency decrease; for LLMs we expect ~5–12% quality delta depending on prompt mix.
- Operational constraints: if the regional pool hits 90% utilization, automatic throttles apply with pre-specified grace periods.

I'll attach an exported capacity sheet showing GPU-hours and probability of denial per percentile. If Synergy wants a guaranteed 4-hour hard cap regardless of region stress, that's doable but requires a reserved ephemeral pool (pre-bought or priced as an option).

Attachment: synergy-capacity-model.xlsx (spreadsheet, 120KB)

—Ben
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@synergyai.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Carlos Ruiz <c.ruiz@synergyai.com>
Date: 2026-09-22T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated sizing question — burst SLAs and entitlements

Hi Neha / Ben,

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the model, Ben. Procurement has three follow-ups before legal will accept the amendment:

1) They want the exact credit formula if we request burst and are denied due to "fleet constraints" — can you propose a concrete example (math) we can put in the SLA?
2) We need clarity on cross-region fallback: will failover incur additional egress/replication costs or is that covered under the Dedicated agreement?
3) Can you confirm whether throughput throttles during high utilization are visible in the Console (so our oncall can triage)?

If possible, please include an explicit example entry in the SLA PDF (we attached a template). We want to avoid vague "pro-rated credits" language.

Appreciate it — Sam
Samantha Lee
Head of Procurement, SynergyAI

Attachment: synergy-sla-template.pdf (pdf, 210KB)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-23T09:16:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: proposed SLA amendment language + next steps

Folks — internal draft we can send to Sam/Carlos. I'm pasting the suggested clause and a simple credit example. Please review and flag changes.

SUGGESTED CLAUSE (Draft):
"Burst Entitlements: Customer is entitled to request burst capacity beyond their committed slab for short windows ("Burst Windows"). Burst Windows up to 4 hours are governed by the following entitlement bands: Standard: up to 2.0x committed slab; Premium: up to 3.5x committed slab when a Reserved Ephemeral Pool is purchased. Burst capacity is subject to overall regional availability and may be denied when Redwood's regional utilization exceeds 90%. In the event of denial due to Redwood capacity constraints, Customer shall receive a Burst Credit calculated as: (Denied GPU-hours) x (Committed GPU Hour Rate) x 0.75. Credits will be applied to the following invoice cycle."

CROSS-REGION / EGRESS: failover to a different region is permitted when configured; egress/replication costs are not covered by default and will be itemized unless the customer purchases a cross-region failover add-on.

OBSERVABILITY: throttles and burst denials are surfaced in Console alerts (burst-denial events) and as a per-route metric. We'll provide a sample dashboard link and an alerting playbook.

Next steps:
- Ben: finalize the capacity-sheet numbers and add the 95th/99th percentile denial probabilities.
- Karthik: confirm whether we need legal sign-off for the specific credit multiplier (0.75) or if 1.0 is safer for enterprise deals.
- Neha: once Ben/Karthik sign off, I'll push this into the SLA PDF and send to Sam/Carlos with the attachments.

Related: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1A2b3Csynergy-capacity-plan

—Aditya Rao
Head of Commercial Operations, Redwood Inference
